source.notes: Achieving high-performance interior permanent magnet machines with reduced rare-earth content typically requires complex topology or shape optimization paired with costly finite element analysis simulations. Bitmap-based surrogate models accelerate the process, however, suffer from substantial data demands for training. To overcome this problem, we explored low-dimensional B'ezier curve-based magnet shaping along with surrogate modeling for a 22-MW generator. Several models including support vector regression, fully connected neural networks, and a novel two-stage surrogate that integrates a least-volume autoencoder with a feedforward neural network were evaluated. The two-stage surrogate framework is shown to achieve a normalized RMSE = 1.0 in prediction errors in several key performance metrics, including demagnetization, efficiency, power, and load torque. A Globol Sobol sensitivity analysis further identified dominant shape- and magnetic features in the design influencing machine performance.
source.title: Surrogate-Based Sensitivity Analysis for Low-Dimensional Freeform Generator Designs: Preprint
